content.comment_body: Hello, In one of the projects, I am using [product_no] with a [product_name] display. The power supply for the panel switches off once or twice daily. In some cases, the program gets erased. We installed an SD card to help solve this, but once, even the program on the SD card was lost. The program is password protected. Can you suggest possible reasons for the program deletion?

Hi, Could you clarify what you mean by "Power switches off once or twice a day"? Is this a controlled shutdown via a switch or contactor, or is it due to an unstable power supply? If the issue is an unreliable power source, the only solution is to stabilize it. Otherwise, it's difficult to predict the outcome of these interruptions. Hope this helps.

The program in the [product_name] is stored on an EEPROM, which can only be cleared intentionally. It’s possible someone is deleting the program manually. If not, the best solution may be to replace your [product_name] with a new one. The same applies to the SD card; the program can only be deleted by choice. If it was lost unexpectedly, the SD card might be defective. Power cycling, whether a couple of times or frequently, should not affect program storage.
It is due to a faulty power supply with fluctuating main voltage. I intend to install a small UPS for the [product_name]. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users encountered unexpected program loss with a [product_name] controller, despite password protection and use of an SD card. This issue aligned with repeated, uncontrolled power interruptions, creating questions about the device's ability to retain program data when power is unstable. Participants expressed concern for the reliability of memory retention under these circumstances.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] controller to reliably maintain program data during unexpected power interruptions. Additional security options like password protection and SD card back-up are anticipated to ensure program persistence.
